text:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's batching-heuristic tweak I'm seeing a sharp tail on padding-heavy requests (seq padding > 1024). Perfetto flame shows lots of long memcpy CPU->GPU spans clustered right before token generation starts.

aj: Can you paste the perfetto view + the nsys command you ran?

maria: attaching quick notes, ran nsys + perfetto on a repro workload: 
```bash
nsys profile --output=run_h2d_spike --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=cudaApi
# then convert + open in perfetto
```
Perfetto timeline: long yellow slices labeled "cudaMemcpyAsync H2D" ~8-14ms each, repeated per-request for padded sequences. Stackframe shows memcpy called from runtime::prepare_input -> allocator->to_device.

liam: interesting — did the heuristic change the batching window so small batches are promoted to a different device path? that can force host staging allocations.

emily: I dug into the allocator logs: after the heuristic change we added a fallback where if batch_size < 4 we go through host-staging path to avoid OOM bursts. looks like for padded seqs that triggers frequently.

maria: logs: 
```
[2025-11-07T14:12:03Z] request_id=xx alloc_path=host_staging size=48MB -> cudaMemcpyAsync H2D
[2025-11-07T14:12:03Z] request_id=yy alloc_path=device_direct size=48MB -> kernel_launch
```

dmitri: ran a quick bisect across the batching heuristic refactor, narrowed to commit 7f3a9c4 (heuristic: prefer low-latency small-batch path -> changed decision threshold from 2->4). reverting locally reproduces the old behavior (memcpy spikes disappear).

aj: can you share before/after numbers? median / p95 / p99?

dmitri: short numbers from synthetic run (padding=1536, batch=1..6):
- before (master@pre-7f3a9c4): median=104ms, p95=370ms, p99=610ms
- after (master@7f3a9c4): median=112ms, p95=980ms, p99=1.6s

maria: the perfetto slices line up with the p95 spikes — every big cudaMemcpyAsync corresponds to a p95 event. it's not a kernel slowdown, it's memory staging.

emily: probable mitigation options: 1) revert threshold change 2) coalesce host copies (batch input staging) 3) pre-allocate pinned pool for tiny batches 4) opt-in flag for legacy path.

aj: ops/rollout note — deploy-bot shows the heuristic change went to canary at 2025-11-06T22:00 UTC, ~5% traffic. If we revert we should hotfix across canary/dedicated quickly.

deploy-bot: :information_source: rollout update: job/heuristic-rollout #342 succeeded to canary (5%). SHA: 7f3a9c4.

liam: quick diagnostic patch that coalesces host staging for padding>512 avoids repeated small memcpys — can we try that in canary?

dmitri: pushed a debug build with pinned pool + coalescing to canary-1, running nsys now. early numbers look promising: p95 dropped to ~400ms. will post trace.

maria: nice, please attach perfetto when ready. after that we can decide revert vs targeted fix. :thumbsup:

aj: also add an automated perf regression test for padded sequences to catch this in presubmit (compare host_staging time, p95 delta).

emily: creating an issue for a proper fix + perf test. tagging infra and QA. :eyes: 

dmitri: posted perfetto link (private): https://perfetto.host/r/trace/abc123

maria: confirmed — new trace shows much shorter H2D spans and larger contiguous device allocations. good signal.

liam: summary: root cause = batching-heuristic threshold change -> more small batches take host_staging path -> repeated cudaMemcpyAsync spikes -> tail latency regressions on padding-heavy workloads. mitigation in canary looks good. next: decide revert vs fix + add presubmit guard.

maria: thanks all — I'll coordinate a rollback if canary numbers don't stay good. keeping this thread for the trace artifacts. :bug:
